findings.summary: The executor regression tests do not verify the explicit ContextVar propagation that replaces asyncio.to_thread semantics.
findings.diagnosis: The production change manually copies the caller context and runs initialization inside it, but every new case uses ordinary mocks and state. Deleting contextvars.copy_context() and context.run from _run_install_and_startup would leave all six new tests and the retained focused suite green, despite changing the former asyncio.to_thread context-propagation contract.
findings.evidence: The parameterized test at lines 136-167 proves default-executor starvation recovery for list, inspect, and validate, but it never sets a ContextVar or observes one inside initialize_di, startup, or cache refresh; no ContextVar coverage for runtime initialization exists elsewhere in tests.
findings.correction: Add a counterfactual case that sets a sentinel ContextVar in the calling task, observes that exact value from initialize_di or _refresh_cache on the lifecycle executor, and would fail if copy_context/context.run were removed.

findings.summary: The starvation regression depends on millisecond polling and a one-second wall-clock completion cutoff.
findings.diagnosis: The test treats failure to finish within one second as proof of executor starvation, while worker readiness is detected by up to 1,000 asyncio.sleep(0.001) polls. A loaded CI host can therefore produce the same result as the deadlock even when the dedicated lifecycle executor is correct.
findings.evidence: wait_for_thread_event loops over asyncio.sleep(0.001) at lines 117-121, and complete_tasks_or_break_counterfactual classifies any task pending after asyncio.wait(..., timeout=1) at lines 125-128 as starved.
findings.correction: Signal worker readiness into an asyncio.Event with loop.call_soon_threadsafe instead of polling, then use a generously bounded outer deadlock guard while asserting the ordering events that distinguish queued lifecycle work from ordinary slow completion.
